newsitem.title: USA: Montana Senate gives nod to electric deregulation.
newsitem.headline: Montana Senate gives nod to electric deregulation.

text.p: The Montana Senate on Friday passed final legislation restructuring the state's electricity industry beginning on July 1, 1998, according to officials at Montana Power Co.
The measure was approved earlier in the week by the Montana House of Representatives and Governor Marc Racicot was expected to sign it next week.

Jack Haffey, chief operating officer for Montana Power energy and communications services, said the legislation represented a compromise between the utility, rural electric cooperatives and consumer groups.
While not "elated" with the bill, "we are pleased to be bringing this kind of legislation to Montana. It is much better to shape competition than to allow it form on an ad hoc basis," he noted.
The approved plan differs from a draft proposed by the utility on several topics including stranded cost recovery and consumer protections.
In addition, Montana Power had envisioned phasing in competition evenly over the transition period, compared with the final bill's pilot program approach.

Under the bill, large industrial customers can choose their power supplier on July 1, 1998; after pilot programs on choice, all residential, commercial and smaller industrial customers will have choice of supplier by July 1, 2002.
The legislation also includes a two-year rate freeze, beginning July 1, 1998, and an additional two-year freeze on the energy component of bills for residential and commercial ratepayers.
The procedure for recovery of stranded costs includes a review of utility cost estimates and efforts to mitigate those costs, by the Montana Public Service Commission.
"We will not be recovering all of our stranded costs in any event," said Perry Cole, Montana Power's vice president of regulatory affairs.
